tess: FYI I hit a reproducible issue in the Next starter: streaming stalls when an ephemeral auth rotates mid-stream.

ali: Thanks — what's the root cause?

tess: The JS SDK attaches the Authorization header once and reuses it for retries. If our short-lived token rotates while the stream is active, a retry reconnects with the stale header and the server ignores it.

ali: Which SDK version in the template?

tess: @redwood/sdk 0.9.2 from the starter template. Python client resolves auth per-retry so it doesn't fail.

ali: Quick mitigation for the starter: do the ephemeral exchange on a server route and return a one-time presigned URL or have the client fetch a fresh token immediately before opening the stream.

tess: Long-term: propose exposing an authResolver callback in the JS client that is invoked on every request/retry (e.g., { auth: async ()=>fetch('/api/ephemeral').then(r=>r.json()).token }). That keeps backwards compatibility while covering edge demos.

dev-bot: Issue created: github.com/redwood/client/issues/412 - add authResolver + e2e test for streaming token rotation.

ali: Great. Please add a short doc blurb in the starter README under "Edge auth patterns" showing authResolver + presigned URL workarounds so new users don't trip over this during onboarding.

tess: Will open starter PR once client change lands. Collecting any other repros (cookie session, self-hosted edge) here.

ali: I'll prototype tests and a patch for 0.9.x after lunch.

tess: :thumbsup:
